title: Emily / Kobi (client working session)

items.topic: Deal currency means operator-to-WagerTech payment
items.statement: The currency field under the deal's commercial terms states the currency in which the operator pays WagerTech (typically USD). It must not be assumed to be the currency WagerTech pays out on the sign-up.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: So the commercial terms of the deal which would be labeled in the currency field don't always match what we would pay have the currency we would pay out to the sign up. So that's just telling you how they're going to pay like what funds they're going to pay us in. And typically they pay us in USDU and it's our affiliates. So that can't be assumed. Currency to currency can't be assumed.

items.topic: Clicks currently all arrive as CAD
items.statement: Kobi stated that all incoming clicks currently come in as CAD regardless of whether the deal is US or Canadian; Emily did not contest this.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um, right now they're all coming in as CAD for all of those clicks. Um, and when we create the signup record from that lick that comes in, um, the currency for that signup, uh, shouldn't be the one from the deal.
items.critic_note: Kept as status-update; the CAD claim is Kobi's own restatement ('let me see if I understand correctly') and Emily only responded to the deal-currency part, so the CAD status is Jumpr's statement, not client-confirmed.

items.topic: Deal market country sets signup payout currency
items.statement: The market country of the deal (not the deal's commercial-terms currency) determines the payout currency for the sign-up. Emily confirmed this when Kobi restated it.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So the market currency for The deal determines the payout currency for the sign / Emily Vandenberg: The market country. / Kobi Kunasekaran: up. / Emily Vandenberg: Yes. For the deal determines the payout / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. / Emily Vandenberg: currency.

items.topic: Deal players only from deal's market country
items.statement: For a deal whose market is Canada, the player can only come from Canada, so the payout is in Canadian currency.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: have signups coming in from like various regions um and not well when I say Canada like the market for the deal is Canada um your payout regardless of where the player comes from is going to be Canadian. / Emily Vandenberg: The player can only come from Canada.

items.topic: Player relocation edge case drives USD payouts
items.statement: Edge case: a player who first signed up on a Canadian book may later move to the US and sign up for US books; those later sign-ups pay the rep and referral in USD. The book defines currency from a payout perspective.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: but we technically could have a player in our ecosystem that has like that they come in as a Canadian like on a Canadian book like the book really defines currency from a payout perspective. um and then maybe two years down the road they move to the US which they're then eligible to sign up for books in the US they would come through and if they signed / Kobi Kunasekaran: Mhm. / Emily Vandenberg: up then the rep's payout would be uh you and like um and the referral / Kobi Kunasekaran: in USD that title. / Emily Vandenberg: USD

items.topic: Stamp currency on signup, not player formula
items.statement: Because of the relocation edge case, signup currency is not derived by a formula from the player; it is stamped on the sign-up record. Emily's reply is cut off at the time, but she later confirms the deal-market-country default for sign-up (lines 193-194, 245-246).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh okay. So that means we shouldn't just uh automatically use formula fields based on player. We need to stamp it on the sign up. / Emily Vandenberg: That's the

items.statement: Jumpr will map deal market country to signup currency: Canada to CAD and US to USD. Emily later confirms Kobi will go with market country from the deal for sign-up.

items.topic: Deal payout currency field if no combined option
items.statement: Kobi said that if the combined US/Canada option is not needed, a payout currency (or similar) on the deal based on market country could be stamped on the sign-up. This is conditional on Emily's check with Joyce.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. If Yeah. If we don't need that option, then it becomes simple like we just map we have like a payout currency or something like that on the deal that's based on the market country and then that's the currency that we would stamp on the signup.

Kobi Kunasekaran: right now we don't I'm just like future thinking because uh we're probably going to have like, you know, total amounts paid paid to the player and things like that added later.

items.topic: Player aggregates convert to base currency
items.statement: Kobi described how future player-level totals would work: amounts in different currencies are added using each currency's conversion rate at the time of aggregation and displayed in the player's base currency. Emily said 'got it'; no build commitment was made.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So when it's being added up it's going to respect each currency's conversion rate at the time that we do the uh the aggregation. And then when it's displayed on the player record, uh it's going to be displayed with the base currency of the player. ... Emily Vandenberg: got / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um so yeah, / Emily Vandenberg: it.

items.topic: Player record has only signup count
items.statement: Kobi stated that the player record currently only has a total signups count (a flat number), so there is no currency concept on the player yet; currency matters only if amounts paid or redeposits are aggregated later.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But then when we like if we want to start doing aggregates, right? Like right now we just have like total signups. So it's just a flat like number of signups. So accounts there's no currency concept.

items.topic: Payout records carry their own currency
items.statement: Kobi explained that payout objects are separate from the player and show whatever currency is set on those payout records; the player currency only governs displayed aggregates. Emily acknowledged with 'Yeah'; no payout design was fixed.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So like the payout objects is separate like whatever currency we set on those records is what going to show up there. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah.

items.topic: Selectable currency for dual-country deals
items.statement: Kobi asked whether there will be deals where the country could be both US and Canada and, if so, whether the currency should be selectable. Emily replied that a deal is defined by the market, country and state combination; the question folds into the open Joyce check (items 10-11).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ... do we are are we going to have deals where uh the country could be both and in that case should we make it selectable / Emily Vandenberg: But the deal is defined by market by the combination of market, country and state.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Payout structures remain based on USD with foreign exchange conversions applied for local disbursements.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: ... the success pay rate for each is in USD and they have a Canadian which is a conversion. Yeah. like the I think the payout module has to handle the like like that when we get there. ... Emily Vandenberg: I can confirm that with Lena.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary states the USD/FX payout structure as settled; in the transcript Emily is unsure while reading contracts and says she will confirm with Lena. Summary is firmer than the transcript.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Future financial aggregations will utilize historical conversion rates to display totals in base currency.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So when it's being added up it's going to respect each currency's conversion rate at the time that we do the uh the aggregation. ... Kobi Kunasekaran: ... if we need to add any other logic later on when we start doing those types of rollups, we can deal with it at that point.
gemini_disagreements.why: Summary turns Kobi's illustrative explanation into a firm plan ('will utilize') and says 'historical conversion rates'; the transcript says the rate at the time of aggregation and defers rollup logic.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: (Details) Kobi Kunasekaran proposed setting the initial player currency based on the player country, making it editable for address changes, while redeposits will follow the deal country's currency (00:14:08).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: level you're just going back you're just redepositing against a deal right and so then you would assume the same currency. / Kobi Kunasekaran: correct. Yeah. / Emily Vandenberg: So like the redeposit will follow the deal
gemini_disagreements.why: Misattribution: the redeposit-follows-deal rule was stated by Emily (client) and agreed by Kobi, not proposed by Kobi.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: (Details) Emily Vandenberg stated they would confirm this payout structure and referral currency configuration with Lena (00:09:39).
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Emily Vandenberg: I can confirm that with Lena. / ... / Kobi Kunasekaran: Cuz like there's also like the concept of like referrals as well, right? And the referral currency that determines the payout or / Emily Vandenberg: yeah and we'll set that we will set that um and that will stay

notes: 17-minute 1:1 on currency logic (sign-up, deal, player, redeposit, payout). No Jira keys spoken. Rule 5: specific referral/success pay-rate amounts read from contracts (line 177/179) not recorded. Joyce and Lena are named but not present; outcomes of those follow-ups are not in this doc. Gemini Decisions/Next steps broadly match the transcript; the Summary hardens the payout/FX structure and the aggregation approach. Critic: read all 269 lines; added 3 items (28-30); fixed quotes on items 17 and 20 ('Okay,' was from line 243); corrected line_end on item 21; annotated item 02; added 1 Gemini disagreement (Lena/referral currency). All other quotes verified verbatim.
